subject: Transit Bridge standby — subprocessor inventory & control questions
messages:
From: Ayesha Khan <legal+vendor@clearline.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transit Bridge Standby: Request for Subprocessor Details and Controls

Hi Jonas,

We heard from our ops team that Clearline traffic for a small set of APAC customers may be routed via a short-lived transit proxy ("TransitBridge") you plan to stand up as a temporary routing/egress assist for the Singapore region. Before we can approve this for production traffic we need a short subprocessor inventory and a few controls/evidence items. Can you please provide the following by close of business PT on 2028-05-22?

- A completed subprocessor inventory (template attached) for TransitBridge and any downstream processors it relies on.
- A one-page dataflow diagram showing ingress -> transitbridge -> onshore fallback (if any).
- Controls summary (encryption, KMS, key custody, access controls, logging/retention).
- SOC2/ISO evidence or equivalent attestations for any 3rd-party subprocessors referenced.
- Confirmation of egress locations (country/region) and whether logs contain PII.

Go-live timeline requested by product is 2028-05-28, so we need to triage this quickly. Point of contact for follow-ups would be helpful.

Thanks,
Ayesha Khan
Senior Counsel, Vendor Risk
Clearline Payments

Attachments: template_subprocessor_inventory.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ayesha Khan <legal+vendor@clearline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transit Bridge Standby: Request for Subprocessor Details and Controls

Hi Ayesha — thanks for the heads up and the template.

Quick summary up front: TransitBridge is an ephemeral transit/egress helper we plan to run with strict ACLs and limited retention for the next two weeks to offload burst routing during the Singapore maintenance window. We own the code and configuration; the only external dependency is a managed connectivity partner for cross-region egress (details below).

We will provide the completed inventory and the controls summary by end-of-day PT 2028-05-22. In the meantime, attaching a short controls summary and the preliminary dataflow diagram so your team can start review.

Key pointers (high level):
- Data types: primarily routing metadata and connection traces. No full request bodies will be stored by TransitBridge; payloads are proxied.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest; keys managed in customer-dedicated KMS (HSM-backed).
- Logs: access and connection logs retained for 7 days, redacted for PII by default.
- Egress: primary: Singapore (SG), fallback: Japan (JP) onshore relay.

Attachments: transitbridge_controls_summary.pdf (pdf), dataflow_apac.png (png)

Point of contact: jonas.weber@redwood.ai; cc'ing Kimberly and Naomi from security & privacy to help with evidence collection.

— Jonas
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@clearline.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ayesha Khan <legal+vendor@clearline.com>
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 08:30:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Transit Bridge Standby: Request for Subprocessor Details and Controls

On Sun, 20 May 2028 at 10:05 -0700, Jonas Weber wrote:
> Quick summary up front: TransitBridge is an ephemeral transit/egress helper we plan to run with strict ACLs...

Thanks for the quick reply Jonas. A couple of clarifying questions from our ops and infosec teams:

1) KMS/KC: You mentioned HSM-backed KMS — is the key material customer-dedicated or shared? Who has administrative access to the keys (Redwood ops only, or third-party KMS operator)?
2) Logs: you said logs are redacted for PII by default — can you confirm whether request/response headers or small amounts of user identifiers are ever written to logs in any error scenarios?
3) Egress jurisdiction: will any payloads transit through the US or EU in the path for APAC customers? We need to confirm cross-border movement.
4) Onshore fallback: what partner will act as the onshore relay in JP and do you have their SOC2 or equivalent?

Also can you confirm whether you are planning any contract-level addendum (DPA) for this temporary routing change? If so please send the DocuSign link for our legal team.

Oliver Park
Vendor Risk — Clearline Payments

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ayesha Khan <legal+vendor@clearline.com>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@clearline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 13:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transit Bridge Standby: Request for Subprocessor Details and Controls

Hi Ayesha / Oliver — answers inline below and attaching a zip with evidence for your review.

1) KMS / Key custody:
- Keys are customer-dedicated keystores within our managed HSM cluster. Redwood has limited operator roles; KMS administration requires multi-person approval. No third-party has direct access to raw key material.

2) Logging and PII: 
- TransitBridge logs only connection metadata (source/dest IP hash, timestamps, latency). We redact user identifiers by default and never persist full request bodies. In an error path we may capture truncated headers for debugging; those are swept within 24 hours and are excluded from any long-term retention.

3) Egress / cross-border routing:
- For APAC traffic the planned path is: client -> TransitBridge (SG) -> onshore-relay (JP) if needed. No routing through EU/US for the affected customer subset. We will provide trace samples to demonstrate path locality.

4) Onshore fallback partner:
- Partner: OnshoreRelay Co. (they are SOC2 Type II; evidence included in the zip).

DPA addendum / contract:
- We have prepared a short DPA addendum for this temporary routing change (covers retention limits, incident notification and subprocessor list). DocuSign link below; the addendum is narrowly scoped for the TransitBridge window.

Attachments (included): standby_evidence.zip (zip) — contains:
- TransitBridge control matrix (PDF)
- OnshoreRelay SOC2 summary (PDF)
- sample redacted traces (txt)
- dataflow_apac.png (png)

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/AAABBB-TransitBridge-DPA-addendum
Drive working folder: https://drive.google.com/redsandbox/transitbridge-dataflow

If you'd like a brief sync (15 min) to walk through the artifacts, I can coordinate with Kimberly / Naomi tomorrow morning PT.

— Jonas
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Ayesha Khan <legal+vendor@clearline.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Park <oliver.park@clearline.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transit Bridge Standby: Request for Subprocessor Details and Controls

Thanks Jonas — that covers the majority of our asks. We'll run a quick internal review of the evidence in standby_evidence.zip and the SOC2 extract from OnshoreRelay. A couple of minor follow-ups:

- Please confirm the 24-hour sweep for any truncated debug headers is automated and auditable (we may ask for a short screenshot of the sweep job logs).
- One retention redline from procurement: can you cap operational log retention to 7 days for this window (we appreciate that's your default, please confirm in the DPA addendum).

We'll review the DocuSign addendum and aim to return a signed copy by 2028-05-24. If procurement requests any small edits we'll route to Naomi.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Ayesha Khan
Senior Counsel, Vendor Risk
Clearline Payments

On the signature: please include your direct phone in case we need a live touchpoint.
